mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate earnings and signals economic slowdown, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in HOUST and a fall in RSAFS over two months signals weakening housing demand and reduced consumer savings, which together depresses consumption and investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 0% MoM and RSAFS < 0% MoM for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decrease in CPIAUCSL over three months signals a restrictive monetary policy that is successfully reducing inflationary pressures, which supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > previous month and CPIAUCSL < previous month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in PAYEMS above trend by more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > trend by >0.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized increase in GDPC1 above 3% for six consecutive quarters signals a strong economic expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 70% of quarters where GDPC1 > 3% YoY for six consecutive quarters.
